inventory.name: Parse processing instructions in HTML (HTML parser change)

inputs.rationale: The parser change exposes no author-supplied input surface: processing instructions are recognised in the HTML source itself, and the page documents no API parameter for the change.

errors.rationale: The page documents no error or failure behaviour for the change: processing instructions were previously silently discarded by the parser, and no exception, fallback, or failure mode is documented anywhere on the page.

lifecycle.rationale: The page documents no author-facing lifecycle for the change: PI nodes are emitted by the parser during parsing, and no creation, observation, or teardown API is documented.

securityPrivacy.rationale: Not documented by this page rather than absent in principle: the page carries no security or privacy statement for parser-preserved processing instructions - no permission, origin, sanitisation, or data-exposure consideration appears on it.

lifecycle.rationale: No lifecycle API is documented for the interface on this page: it shows no creation, cloning, observation, or removal surface - only parser emission and DOM traversal.

notes: IDS: the page previously had NO heading ids - the census's ids=3 were escaped text inside the code example (id="content", id="chunk-1" twice), not anchors. Added five ids on h2 headings only (the page has no h3, so no fragment resolves to nothing): syntax on 'shape of the API', context on 'what processing instructions are', examples on 'example', browser-support on 'browser support', see-also on 'see also'. The canonical three come from the brief; context and examples were added because the context and examples dimensions must resolve to fragments whose slices actually contain that content (the examples slice is the page's only <pre>). No code block was added - the census's pre=1 is the pre-existing example block. INVENTORY is the page's own documented surface: the parser change, the ProcessingInstruction interface, and the three rows of the page's shape table; Node.PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE (nodeType 7) is a pre-existing Node constant, inventoried because the page documents it as the detection member of this surface. NOT-APPLICABLE PATTERN: inputs, errors, lifecycle and securityPrivacy are not-applicable on every row, each naming what the page does not document - no author input surface, no exception or failure behaviour, no creation/observation/teardown API, and no security or privacy statement anywhere on the page. SOURCE GAPS NOT WRITTEN INTO THE PAGE (drafted for the implementer, reading date 2026-10-07, both sources fetched and HTTP 200): (1) the ChromeStatus summary and DOM Standard 4.13 both give ProcessingInstruction an element-like attribute API to mutate data (constructor, hasAttributes, getAttributeNames, getAttribute, setAttribute, removeAttribute, toggleAttribute, hasAttribute) that the page's shape table omits entirely; (2) the page's Firefox standards position says 'No signal' while the ChromeStatus record reads ff view 'Positive' (mozilla/standards-positions issue 1369); (3) the page's status cells say 'Enabled by default' while the ChromeStatus headline status reads 'Proposed' (val 2) with desktop/android/webview milestones all 150 - the milestones corroborate the page's 'Chrome 150+'/'All platforms' framing, the status text does not. COVERAGE OMISSION (verified against sources 2026-10-07): the page's shape table lists target, data and nodeType only, while the ChromeStatus summary and the DOM IDL both describe an attribute API for mutating processing-instruction data. The source adds a qualifier the page does not carry; that is an omission rather than a two-sided contradiction, so it is recorded here and deliberately NOT disclosed as a disagreement.
